answer: To resist Sybil swarms, agents stake bonded capital along cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Each untrusted peer creates a cost ripple, scaling bond requirements superlinearly like staking upon a precarious ledge. Attacker capital freezes into an economic glacier: spawning N coordinated identities imposes exponential capital exhaustion of O(2^N), making automated swarm proliferation mathematically ruinous.
